The slide's project-results table, kept by the build: scripts/ai-usage-ledger.mjs --check fails when a decision record lands without its line. Numbers here are never typed from memory: wallClockHours come from git commit timestamps; sessionTokensObserved is the harness's own budget counter, read, not guessed; tokens per task are null where no meter exposes them, and that is said rather than filled.

Token use not instrumented; honest estimate about 2.0M, read-heavy - the 5.5MB course file region, seven gate and helper modules, the KJV corpus for 40 verses, three rounds of measure-and-repair on the band ladder. The 40h without-AI estimate is for the same artifact at the same standard: about 90,000 characters of teaching prose across five reader registers, 40 verses fetched and pinned verbatim, a 55-case proven-to-catch gate, a record and a session note. The local full vitest run spent roughly 35 minutes queued behind two sibling runs on the machine's two-slot memory brake; that wait is in the wall figure but is not compute this build used. Three faults in my own work were caught by my own gate rather than by reading: a British spelling in anchor.theme prose, the bare phrase 'the teacher' in a child-band school illustration, and a quiz distractor naming Bishop Gwin for a send that names nobody - the exact DR-0719 fault sov70 and sov71 had already recorded.

entries.task: Give two dormant lanes a voice: the lesson-mail watcher says what its dormancy costs, and the email door reports mail-password presence before the tailnet gate
entries.notes: Found while reading the Gmail intake queue for the next oldest-first lesson: 39 uncaptured threads, nine of the first thirty already shipped. Measured the cause rather than assuming it - lesson-mail-watch.yml has 480 runs from 2026-08-25 to 2026-11-09 and every sampled run was an honest no-op, so the automated Gmail door has never once opened. The estimate without AI is the cost of noticing at all: the fact was visible only in the raw log of run 480.

entries.task: Teach the ledger resolver to own the two budget ratchets: union the append-only raises and re-base ours onto main's chain
entries.notes: The two ratchet files conflict on every landing and were resolved by hand twice the same day, which is quadratic in open branches. The resolver unions raises, re-bases our entries keeping each delta, and defers the ceiling to each guard's own down-only --generate and check so it never invents a measurement. 11 new checks on the real 2026-11-06 numbers; one expected-refusal check proved the code wrong rather than the test.
